title: Hall Wall Crossing and Physical BPS Dictionary

items.title: Pure SU(2) physical BPS charge and index data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; exact proof/source contract and readiness disposition are recorded in batch 54 evidence.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets. Let $U$ be a simply connected regular patch of its source-proposed Seiberg–Witten Coulomb branch on which the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. The earlier Coulomb-branch data define the formal charge-label lattice $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with labels $\gamma=(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing $\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The source-proposed model convention fixes the scalar central charge to be $z_u(\gamma)=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)$; $a,a_D,z_u$ have mass dimension one, $u$ has mass dimension two, and charge labels and pairings are dimensionless.

For the model-specific physical charge data used here, equip $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ with the integral antisymmetric Dirac pairing

$$\langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_m n'_e-n_e n'_m).$$

In particular the source-designated monopole label $\gamma_m=(0,1)$ and dyon label $\gamma_d=(1,-1)$ satisfy $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2$, the convention matched by a two-arrow Kronecker quiver with both arrows directed from the dyon vertex to the monopole vertex. The lattice records formal charge labels only: it does not assert that every label is an allowed line operator or a realized particle.

For each $u\in U$, the selected model supplies a stable support $\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\gamma\in\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$, supply an abstract one-particle massive rest-fiber Hilbert sector $\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ with positive inner product linear in its first variable, a bounded self-adjoint grading involution, a positive rest mass $M_{u,\gamma}$, and the conserved label $\gamma$. On a supplied common dense graded invariant domain $\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$, supply the $\mathcal N=2$ supertranslation representation of the earlier BPS-state definition: $P^0=M_{u,\gamma}I$, $P^j=0$, $Z^{12}=z_u(\gamma)I$, $Z^{21}=-z_u(\gamma)I$, and closed odd supercharges $Q^I_\alpha$ with their actual Hilbert adjoints, with every product in the bracket table defined there. Use metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so $P_0=-M_{u,\gamma}I$. This fiber is not asserted to be a normalizable fixed-momentum subspace of a full super-Poincaré Hilbert representation.

The spin-cover Lorentz action on vectors is characterized by $\Phi(\Lambda_gx)=g\Phi(x)g^\dagger$ for $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$ and $\Phi(x)=-\sigma^\mu x_\mu$, as in the unitary representation definition. For the rest vector $P_{u,\gamma}=(M_{u,\gamma},0,0,0)$ define its stabilizer
$$G_{P_{u,\gamma}}:=\{g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C):\Lambda_gP_{u,\gamma}=P_{u,\gamma}\}=\mathrm{SU}(2).$$
Indeed $\Phi(P_{u,\gamma})=M_{u,\gamma}I_2$, so the stabilizer condition is $gg^\dagger=I_2$. Separately supply a grading-preserving unitary representation $\pi_{u,\gamma}:\mathrm{SU}(2)\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma})$, meaning $\pi(gh)=\pi(g)\pi(h)$, $\pi(I)=I$, and $\pi(g)^*\pi(g)=I=\pi(g)\pi(g)^*$. Require strong continuity: $g\mapsto\pi(g)\psi$ is norm-continuous for every $\psi$. Require $\pi(g)\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}=\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$ and, on that domain,
$$\pi(g)Q^I_\alpha\pi(g)^{-1}=\sum_\beta g^\beta{}_{\alpha}Q^I_\beta,\qquad \pi(g)(Q^I_\alpha)^*\pi(g)^{-1}=\sum_\beta\overline{g^\beta{}_{\alpha}}(Q^I_\beta)^*,$$
where $g^\beta{}_{\alpha}$ is row $\beta$, column $\alpha$; scalar momenta and central charges are unchanged. This is supplied rest-fiber rotation data, not a restriction of an unspecified full-space operator $U(g,0)$. Choose the spin axis $3$ and the one-parameter rotation subgroup
$$r_3(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\theta/2}&0\\0&e^{i\theta/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z).$$
Supply a nonzero closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ invariant under this supplied $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ action and identified as the selected BPS sector. Its vectors lie in $\mathcal D_{u,\gamma}$. Require the grading involution to preserve this subspace and, for every $I,\alpha$, require $Q^I_\alpha\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$ and $(Q^I_\alpha)^*\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$; thus the selected sector includes every supercharge partner of each of its states. Every nonzero vector is BPS-saturated in the exact sense of the earlier BPS-state definition: $M_{u,\gamma}=|z_u(\gamma)|$, and the two $\mathcal N=2$ annihilating supercharge combinations in that definition vanish on them. Stability is supplied model data: this sector is discrete and separated by a positive spectral gap from the multiparticle continuum at the same conserved charge. The sector and gap are inputs, not conclusions here. On $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$, supply a self-adjoint operator $J_3$ with $2J_3$-integer spectrum such that the restricted action of $r_3(\theta)$ is $e^{-i\theta J_3}$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$. Require its spectral calculus to define a bounded trace-class operator $B_{u,\gamma}=(-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2$, and supply a Hilbert basis $E_{u,\gamma}$ of $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$.

Define the four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ second-helicity supertrace, also called the $B_2$ index here, by

$$\Omega_u(\gamma)=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}(B_{u,\gamma}),$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}$ is the absolutely convergent supplied-basis trace of a trace-class operator; basis independence is not needed here. Set $\Omega_u(\gamma)=0$ for $\gamma\notin\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$. The trace convention uses only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the stated mathematical suppliers, not full Choice. No existence or local constancy of this support is asserted.

Let $\mathcal C\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$ be any chosen set of charges, and fix $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. At each $u\in U$ for which $e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ for every $\gamma\in\mathcal C$, define $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi\in(0,1)$ for $\gamma\in\mathcal C$. For two charges $\gamma,\delta$ with nonzero central charges, define their marginal-stability wall by

$$W_{\gamma,\delta}:=\{u\in U:z_u(\gamma)/z_u(\delta)\in\mathbb R_{>0}\}.$$

Given a specified family $\mathscr W$ of such wall subsets of $U$, a chamber relative to $\mathscr W$ is a connected component of $U\setminus\bigcup_{W\in\mathscr W}W$. A formal positive cone $\Gamma_+\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ used for ordered products contains $0$, is closed under addition, and is pointed ($\Gamma_+\cap(-\Gamma_+)=\{0\}$). It is supplied with an additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ that is positive on nonzero charges and has finite sublevel sets, meaning $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\in\mathbb N$. The definition is conditional on the existence of the Hilbert sectors, trace data, cone, and degree; it constructs no continuum theory and makes no Hall-index identification.

items.physical_scope: Conditional data definition for electric and magnetic charge labels, second-helicity BPS indices, and marginal-stability walls and chambers relative to a supplied wall family in an already specified pure four-dimensional rigid N=2 SU(2) quantum or regulated one-particle model on regular Seiberg–Witten patches; it asserts no state existence, continuum QFT construction, or physical realization of Hall counts.
items.axiom_base: ZF + AC_omega, inherited through the supplied BPS-state, trace-class, and trace definitions.

items.title: Conditional physical BPS wall crossing from an exact Hall bridge
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; exact proof/source contract and readiness disposition are recorded in batch 54 evidence.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the supplied trace-class BPS-index data. Use the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets, in natural units $c=\hbar=1$. On a simply connected regular patch $U$, the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and satisfy $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. Its formal charge-label lattice is $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with
$$z_u(n_e,n_m)=\sqrt2\bigl(n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)\bigr),\qquad \langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_mn'_e-n_en'_m).$$
For each supplied stable one-particle BPS rest sector, $\Omega_u(\gamma)$ is the second-helicity trace $-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}\!\bigl((-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2\bigr)$ from the physical charge-data definition; it is set to zero off the selected stable support. Let $u_-,u_+\in U$ be two specified points.

The finite-field Hall input is a finite acyclic quiver $Q$ over $\mathbb F_q$, where $q>1$ is a prime power. For integer dimension vectors, define
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d),\qquad t=\sqrt q>0.$$

Suppose an additive map $\rho:\mathbb Z^{Q_0}\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and a physical charge cone $\Gamma_+$ are supplied, where $\Gamma_+$ contains $0$, is closed under addition and is pointed, such that $\rho(\mathbb N^{Q_0})\subseteq\Gamma_+$. Supply a positive additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ with finite sublevel sets and require $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$ for every $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$. Assume also, for all $\mathbf d,\mathbf e\in\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$, that

$$\langle\rho(\mathbf d),\rho(\mathbf e)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=\langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q.$$

Let $\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$. Choose one real phase rotation $\alpha$ such that for both $u\in\{u_-,u_+\}$ the vertex charges $Z_u(\mathbf e_i)=e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf e_i))$ lie in $\mathbb H$, and extend each assignment additively by $Z_u(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i Z_u(\mathbf e_i)=e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf d))$. 
A representation $M$ assigns a finite-dimensional $\mathbb F_q$-vector space to each vertex and a linear map to each arrow; its dimension vector is $\mathbf d(M)\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$. The additive central charge $Z_u(\mathbf d)$ was specified above. For nonzero $\mathbf d$, set $\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d)=\arg Z_u(\mathbf d)/\pi\in(0,1)$; this range follows because a nonzero sum of upper-half-plane vertex charges lies in $\mathbb H$. For every nonzero dimension vector, the defining equality for $Z_u$ identifies $\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d)$ with $\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf d)))/\pi$. A nonzero $M$ is $Z_u$-semistable when every nonzero subrepresentation $U\subseteq M$ satisfies $\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d(U))\le\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d(M))$.

On the isomorphism-class basis $\delta_M$, the subobject-first Hall product is $(f\star g)(L)=\sum_{U\subseteq L}f(U)g(L/U)$, with distinct embedded subobjects counted separately. Complete by total dimension, that is, take the product over dimension vectors of the finite-dimensional homogeneous components. For a phase $\phi$, put $S_{Z_u}(\phi)=\delta_0+\sum_{[M]\ne[0],\,M\ Z_u\text{-semistable},\,\phi_{Z_u}(\mathbf d(M))=\phi}\delta_M$, where $\delta_0$ is the Hall unit. Its skew integration is $J(f)=\sum_{[M]}t^{\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(M))}f(M)|\operatorname{Aut}(M)|^{-1}x^{\mathbf d(M)}$, and the completed skew torus has product $x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e}=t^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle_Q}x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}$. The resulting Hall spectrum generator is the decreasing-phase product $P_{Z_u}^{\mathrm{sk}}=\mathop{*}_{\phi}^{\searrow}J(S_{Z_u}(\phi))$, with the largest phase leftmost.

For each of the two specified points define the nonzero index support
$$\Sigma_u:=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+\setminus\{0\}:\Omega_u(\gamma)\ne0\}.$$
Assume $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}:\Omega_u(\gamma)\ne0\}\subseteq\Gamma_+$ for both specified points, so $\Sigma_u$ is the full nonzero index support. Assume $\{\gamma\in\Sigma_u:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\ge0$, $\Omega_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb Z$ on $\Sigma_u$, and $e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb H$ for every $u\in\{u_-,u_+\}$ and $\gamma\in\Sigma_u$. Thus every phase $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi$ used below is defined. Zero charge is excluded from $\Sigma_u$ and from all phase-indexed products.

Let $K_{\mathrm{phys}}$ be a coefficient field with a field embedding $\sigma:\mathbb Q(t)\to K_{\mathrm{phys}}$, and write $v:=\sigma(t)$ for the dimensionless Hall coefficient parameter. Here $\mathbb Q(t)=\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)$ is the field generated by the specified algebraic number $t$, so $v^2=q$ and $v\ne1$; $v$ is distinct from the physical constant $\hbar=1$ fixed by natural units. Use the supplied additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ with $\ell(0)=0$, $\ell(\gamma)>0$ for $\gamma\ne0$, and finite sublevel sets. Define the commutative formal charge-series algebra and the quantum charge torus by

$$\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}:=\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma_+}K_{\mathrm{phys}}y^\gamma,\qquad y^\gamma y^\delta=y^{\gamma+\delta},$$

$$\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}:=\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma_+}K_{\mathrm{phys}}Y^\gamma,\qquad Y^\gamma\star_v Y^\delta=v^{-\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}Y^{\gamma+\delta}.$$

For either algebra and $N\ge0$, let $F^N$ consist of series supported on charges $\gamma$ with $\ell(\gamma)\ge N$. Give both algebras the linear topology whose neighborhoods of zero are the $F^N$. Finite sublevel sets make every truncation modulo $F^N$ finite-dimensional; the algebras are separated and complete, and their products are degreewise finite. Give $\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}^\times$ the subspace topology from $\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}$. For each $N\ge1$, let $G_N$ be the group of $K_{\mathrm{phys}}$-algebra automorphisms of $\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}/F^N$ preserving every induced quotient filtration subspace $F^j/F^N$ for $1\le j<N$, with reduction as the transition maps and the discrete topology on each $G_N$. Define $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{fil}}(\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}):=\varprojlim_{N\ge1}G_N$ with the inverse-limit topology. It is the group of continuous automorphisms and continuous inverses preserving the degree filtration.

The charge map and coefficient embedding define the degree-continuous torus map, extended from the total-dimension-completed Hall skew torus by continuity,

$$\Phi(x^{\mathbf d})=Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)},\qquad \Phi(c x^{\mathbf d})=\sigma(c)Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)}.$$

The degree identity $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$ for $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ ensures this continuity. On the commutative completed charge series, supply a sign refinement $\varepsilon:\Gamma_+\to\{\pm1\}$ with $\varepsilon(0)=1$ and $\varepsilon(\gamma+\delta)=(-1)^{\langle\gamma,\delta\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}\varepsilon(\gamma)\varepsilon(\delta)$. Define the physical KS factor for each $\gamma\in\Sigma_u$ by

$$\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}(y^\delta)=y^\delta\bigl(1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma\bigr)^{\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}.$$

The integer power is interpreted by its formal binomial series in the degree topology. When charges have equal phase, order their labels lexicographically as integer pairs $(n_e,n_m)$. Let $\mathcal S_u$ be the composition of these factors over $\Sigma_u$ in decreasing phase order, with the largest phase leftmost and the stated lexicographic order within each phase. Finally assume an exact model-specific bridge: there is a continuous group homomorphism
$$\Theta:\widehat{\mathbb T}_{\mathrm{phys}}^\times\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{fil}}(\widehat{\mathbb A}_{\mathrm{phys}}),$$
and for every phase $\phi$ and either specified point it satisfies, using the same within-phase order,
$$\Theta\!\left(\Phi(J(S_{Z_u}(\phi)))\right)=\prod_{\substack{\gamma\in\Sigma_u\\\phi_u(\gamma)=\phi}}^{\searrow}\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}.$$

Here $S_{Z_u}(\phi)$ and $J$ are the semistable phase factor and skew integration from the finite-field Hall definition. Then

$$\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}.$$

This is a conditional transport theorem. The specified per-phase bridge is an additional physical input; neither the finite-field Hall identity nor this theorem asserts that the pure-SU(2) model supplies it, that the resulting index counts exist, or that the model has a continuum quantum-field-theory construction.

items.physical_scope: Conditional identity for the second-helicity BPS index of an already specified pure four-dimensional rigid N=2 SU(2) model at two points of a regular Coulomb-branch patch, provided a finite-quiver presentation with finite charge-degree sublevels and an exact coefficient-, charge-, pairing-, and factor-preserving Hall-to-Hilbert bridge are supplied; it asserts neither that this bridge exists nor a continuum QFT construction.
